verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              ततः स सात्यकिर्धीमान्महात्मा वृष्णिपुङ्गवः। सुदर्शनं निहत्याजौ यन्तारं पुनरब्रवीत् ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Thereafter that illustrious scion of the Vrishni race, the high-souled and intelligent Satyaki, having slain Sudarsana in battle, addressing charioteer thus spoke.

verses.sanskrit: रथाश्वनागकलिलं शरशक्त्यूर्मिमालिनम्। खड्गमत्स्यं गदाग्राहं शूरायुधमहास्वनम् ॥२॥
प्राणापहारिणं रौद्रं वादित्रोत्क्रुष्टनादितम्। योधानामसुखस्पर्शं दुर्धर्षमजयैषिणाम् ॥३॥
तीर्णाः स्म दुस्तरं तात द्रोणानीकमहार्णवम्। जलसन्धबलेनाजौ पुरुषादैरिवावृतम् ॥४॥
verses.english: Having crossed the almost uncrossable ocean of Drona's division abounding with chariots and steeds and elephants-ocean of which the waves are constituted by arrows and darts, fishes by swords and scimitars and alligators by the maccs; which roars with the whizz of arrows and the clash of diverse weapons, an ocean that is fierce and destructive of life and resounds with the din created by diverse musical instruments; of which the touch is disagreeable and unbearable to warriors longing to have victory and of which the banks infested by flesh-eaters represented by the forces of Jalasandha, I consider that the remaining of the array yet to be crossed, can be crossed with great ease, like a stream-let of shallow water. Therefore do you dauntlessly drive the steeds forwards.

verses.sanskrit: अतोऽन्यत् पृतनाशेषं मन्ये कुनदिकामिव। तर्तव्यामल्पसलिलां चोदयाश्वानसंभ्रमम्॥५॥
हस्तप्राप्तमहं मन्ये सांप्रतं सव्यसाचिनम्। निर्जित्य दुर्धरं द्रोणं सपदानुगमाहवे॥६॥
हार्दिक्यं योधवर्यं च मन्ये प्राप्तं धनञ्जयम्। न हि मे जायते त्रासो दृष्ट्वा सैन्यान्यनेकशः॥७॥
वह्नेरिव प्रदीप्तस्य वने शुष्कतृणोलपे। पश्य पाण्डवमुख्येन यातां भूमिं किरीटिना॥८॥
verses.english: For a raging forests conflagration shrinks not at the sight of numerous heaps of dried grass. Behold the ground through which the diadem-decked Arjuna, that best of the Pandavas has passed.

verses.sanskrit: पत्त्यश्वरथनागौघैः पतितैर्विषमीकृताम्।  द्रवते तद्यथा सैन्यं तेन भग्नं महात्मना ॥९॥
verses.english: Rendered uneven by the slain foot-soldiers, horses, car-warriors and elephants. Yonder the Kaurava array is giving way being routed by that high-souled warrior.

verses.sanskrit: रथैर्विपरिधावद्भिर्गजैरश्वैश्च सारथे। कौशेयारुणसङ्काशमेतदुद्धूयते रजः॥१०॥
verses.english: O charioteer, behold a thick tawny cloud of dust raised by the flying cars, elephants and steeds.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्याशस्थमहं मन्ये श्वेताश्वं कृष्णसारथिम्। स एष श्रूयते शब्दो गाण्डीवस्यामितौजसः॥११॥
यादृशानि निमित्तानि मम प्रादुर्भवन्ति वै। अनस्तंगत आदित्ये हन्ता सैन्धवमर्जुनः॥१२॥
verses.english: From the omens that are revealing themselves to me, I can judge that Arjuna will slay the ruler of the Sindhus before the sun today goes below the horizon.

verses.sanskrit: शनैर्विश्रम्भयन्नश्वान् याहि यत्रारिवाहिनी। यत्रैते सतलत्राणाः सुयोधनपुरोगमाः॥१३॥
verses.english: Without exhausting their strength, drive the steeds slowly to the spot where the hostile ranks are staying, that is, to the spot where yonder warriors headed by Duryodhana, their hands cased in leathern fences

verses.sanskrit: दंशिताः क्रूरकर्माणः काम्बोजा युद्धदुर्मदाः। शरबाणासनधरा यवनाश्च प्रहारिणः॥१४॥
verses.english: And yonder Kambojas of dreadful deeds, cased in mail and difficult of defeat in battle and these Yavanas armed with bows and arrows and accomplished in smiting.

verses.sanskrit: शकाः किराता दरदा बर्बरास्ताम्रलिप्तकाः। अन्ये च बहवो म्लेच्छा विविधायुधपाणयः॥१५॥
यत्रैते सतलत्राणाः सुयोधनपुरोगमाः। मामेवाभिमुखाः सर्वे तिष्ठन्ति समरार्थिनः॥१६॥
verses.english: To the spot (I repeat) where yonder warriors headed by Duryodhana, their hands defended by leathern gloves, are standing with their faces turned towards me and inspired with the resolution of encountering me.

verses.sanskrit: एतान् सरथनागाश्वान्निहत्याजौ सपत्तिनः। इदं दुर्गं महाघोरं तीर्णमेवोपधारय॥१७॥
verses.english: Consider me, O charioteer as already passed through this dreadful strong-hold, having slain in battle all these warriors and cars, elephants, horses and foot-soldiers that are among them.

verses.sanskrit:
सूत उवाच।
              न संभ्रमो मे वार्ष्णेय विद्यते सत्यविक्रम।  यद्यपि स्यात्तव क्रुद्धो जामदग्न्योऽग्रतः स्थितः॥१८॥
verses.english: The Charioteer said O scion of the Vrishni race, fear I have none, O you of prowess incapable of being withstood! If you had before you the enraged son of Yamadagni.

verses.sanskrit: द्रोणो वा रथिनां श्रेष्ठः कृपो मद्रेश्वरोऽपि वा। तथापि संभ्रमो न स्यात्त्वामाश्रित्य महाभुज॥१९॥
त्वया सुबहवो युद्धे निर्जिताः शत्रुसूदन। दंशिताः क्रूरकर्माणः काम्बोजा युद्धदुर्मदाः॥२०॥
verses.english: O slayer of hostile heroes, numerous Kambojas covered in coats of mail, of dreadful deeds and difficult of defeat in battle, have already been worsted by you;

verses.sanskrit: शरबाणासनधरा यवनाश्च प्रहारिणः। शकाः किराता दरदा बर्बरास्ताम्रलिप्तकाः॥२१॥
verses.english: As also numerous Yavanas armed with bow and arrows and accomplished in smiting, including Sakas, Kiratas, Daradas Barbars, Tamraliptakas.

verses.sanskrit: अन्ये च बहवो म्लेच्छा विविधायुधपाणयः। न च मे संभ्रमः कश्चिद्भूतपूर्वः कथञ्चन॥२२॥
verses.english: And many other Miechchas, armed with various weapons. Never did I feel fear in any battle.

verses.sanskrit: किमुतैतत् समासाद्य धीरसंयुगगोष्पदम्। आयुष्मन् कतरेण त्वां प्रापयामि धनञ्जयम्॥२३॥
verses.english: O you of great courage, why shall I then experience any fear in this battle, which is like the vestige of a cow's hoof. O long-lived one, by which track shall I carry you to the spot where Dhananjaya is?

verses.sanskrit: केषां क्रुद्धोऽसि वार्ष्णेय केषां मृत्युरुपस्थितः। केषां संयमनीमद्य गन्तुमुत्सहते मनः॥२४॥
verses.english: On whom have you been angry, O you of the Vrishni race? Who are they for whom death is waiting? Who are they that are destined to repair to the mansion of death today?

verses.sanskrit: के त्वां युधि पराक्रान्तं कालान्तकयमोपमम्।  दृष्ट्वा विक्रमसंपन्नं विद्रविष्यन्ति संयुगे॥२५॥
केषां वैवस्वतो राजा स्मरतेऽद्य महाभुज। सात्यकिरुवाच। मुण्डानेतान् हनिष्यामि दानवानिव वासवः॥२६॥
verses.english: Satyaki said I will slay these warriors with sharpened shafts like Vasava slaying the Danavas. Slaying the Kambojas, I will fulfill my vow. Carry me thither.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिक्षां पारयिष्यामि काम्बोजानेव मां वह। अद्यैषां कदनं कृत्वा प्रियं यास्यामि पाण्डवम्॥२७॥
verses.english: Today crushing the foe I shall repair to that son of Pandu who is dearly loved my me. Today the Kurus with Suyodhana at their head, will bchold my prowess in battle.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य द्रक्ष्यन्ति मे वीर्यं कौरवाः ससुयोधनाः। मुण्डानीके हते सूत सर्वसैन्येषु चासकृत्॥२८॥
अद्य कौरवसैन्यस्य दीर्यमाणस्य संयुगे। श्रुत्वा विरावं बहुधा सन्तप्स्यति सुयोधनः॥२९॥
verses.english: When this division of the Mlecnchas of shaved heads will be exterminated and the entire Kaurava army put to great distress. Hearing the loud lamentation of the Kaurava host today lacerated and shattered by me in battle, Suyodhana will be filled with great fcar. Today I shall show to my precep:or. the highsouled Pandava of white horse skill in in use of weapons acquired by fie from him Beholding today thousands of forcnes: warriors slain with Duryodhana will be overwhelmed with 21. The Kauravas will this day bozoid the bow in my hand to resemble a circle of fire whe:1, nav arrows. string for discharging my numerous arrows. Beholding the continuous carnage of his troops bathed in blood and many filled all over with shafts, Suyodhana today will be filled with great grief. When I shall slay the best of the Kuru warriors wrathfully.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य पाण्डवमुख्यस्य श्वेताश्वस्य महात्मनः। आचार्यस्य कृतं मार्गं दर्शयिष्यामि संयुगे ॥३०॥
अद्य मद्बाणनिहतान् योधमुख्यान् सहस्रशः। दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो राजा पश्चात्तापं गमिष्यति ॥३१॥
verses.bhavadeepa: श्वेताश्वस्य सकाशे कृतमभ्यस्तं मार्गमस्त्रशिक्षामाचार्यस्य द्रोणस्य दर्शयिष्यामीत्यन्वयः । अथवा आचार्यस्य विद्योपदेष्टुः श्वेताश्वस्य दर्शयिष्यामीति सामान्यकर्मकम् ॥३०॥

verses.sanskrit: अद्य मे क्षिप्रहस्तस्य क्षिपतः सायकोत्तमान्। अलातचक्रप्रतिमं धनुर्द्रक्ष्यन्ति कौरवाः॥३२॥
मत्सायकचिताङ्गानां रुधिरं स्रवतां मुहुः। सैनिकानां वधं दृष्ट्वा सन्तप्स्यति सुयोधनः॥३३॥
अद्य में क्रुद्धरूपस्य निघ्नतश्च वरान् वरान्। द्विरर्जुनमिमं लोकं मंस्यतेऽद्य सुयोधनः॥३४॥
verses.english: Suyodhana will today behold the world to contain two Arjunas. Beholding thousands of kings slain by me in battle, king Duryodhana will be overwhelmed with grief in this day's great fight. Slaying thousands of monarchs today, I will show love and devotion to those high-souled ones viz., the sons of Pandu. Today the Kauravas will know the extent of my prowess and energy and my gratefulness to the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य राजसहस्राणि निहतानि मया रणे। दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो राजा सन्तप्स्यति महामृधे॥३५॥
अद्य स्नेहं च भक्तिं च पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। हत्वा राजसहस्त्राणि दर्शयिष्यामि राजसु॥३६॥

बलं वीर्यं कृतज्ञत्वं मम ज्ञास्यन्ति कौरवाः।
              सञ्जय उवाच।
              एवमुक्तस्तदा सूतः शिक्षितान् साधुवाहिनः॥३७॥
शशाङ्कसन्निकाशान्वै वाजिनो व्यनुदद्भृशम्। ते पिबन्त इवाकाशं युयुधानं हयोत्तमाः॥३८॥
प्रापयन् यवनाञ्शीघ्रं मनःपवनरंहसः। सात्यकिं ते समासाद्य पृतनास्वनिवर्तिनम्॥३९॥
verses.english: Those excellent steeds, possessed of the fleetness of the wind or the mind, dashed forward scanning to devour the very skies and bore Yuyudhana to the spot where those Vas were,

verses.sanskrit: बहवो लघुहस्ताश्च शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्। तेषामिषूनथास्त्राणि वेगवान्नतपर्वभिः॥४०॥
verses.english: Then thosc Yavanas endued with great lightness of hunds obtaining in their midst the unretreating Satyaki, began to cover him with mighty showers of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: अच्छिनत् सात्यकी राजन्नैनं ते प्राप्नुवञ्शराः। रुक्मपुङ्खैः सुनिशितैर्गार्ध्रपत्रैरजिह्मगैः॥४१॥
verses.english: Then Satyaki who was moving with great celerity, cul-off their arrows and weapons with his shafts of depressed knots. Indeed the arrows discharged by them could not then reach him.

verses.sanskrit: उच्चकर्त शिरांस्युग्रो यवनानां भुजानपि। शैक्यायसानि वर्माणि कांस्यानि च समन्ततः॥४२॥
verses.english: The fierce Satyaki then began to lop off the heads and arms of the Yavanas, with sharp arrows cquipt with golden wings or wings made of vultering feathers, all-flying straight.

verses.sanskrit: भित्त्वा देहांस्तथा तेषां शरा जग्मुर्महीतलम्। ते हन्यमाना वीरेण म्लेच्छाः सात्यकिना रणे ॥४३॥
verses.english: Those arrows, penetrating through the iron or brass armours of the Yavanas as also their bodies, then fell down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit: शतशोऽभ्यपतंस्तत्र व्यसवो वसुधातले। सुपूर्णायतमुक्तैस्तानव्यवच्छिन्नपिण्डितैः॥४४॥
verses.english: Thus slaughtered by the heroic Satyaki in that haitle, the Mlechchas began to fall by inundreds on the ground deprived of their lives.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्च षट् सप्त चाष्टौ च बिभेद यवनाञ्शरैः।  काम्बोजानां सहस्रैश्च शकानां च विशांपते॥४५॥
verses.english: With his arrows disc!larged from his bow drawn to the fullest exicnt and flying in a continuous line, that brave warrior began to slay, five, six, seven or eight Yavanas at a time.

verses.sanskrit: शबराणां किरातानां बर्बराणां तथैव च। अगम्यरूपां पृथिवीं मांसशोणितकर्दमाम्॥४६॥
verses.english: Strewn with carcasses and corpses of elephants, horses, car-warriors and heroes, the field, O monarch, became miry with flesh and blood. Huge cars with wheels and without wheels ard having their riders on, were thrown up by elephants, being smashed with the point of their tusks.

verses.sanskrit: कृतवांस्तत्र शैनेयः क्षपयंस्तावकं बलम्। दस्यूनां सशिरस्त्राणैः शिरोभिर्लूनमूर्धजैः॥४७॥
verses.english: The carth became impassable; and it was slippery with the flesh and blond that then constitutcoins mire. The grandson of Sini then cabut carnage amous pour troops.

verses.sanskrit: दीर्घकूर्चैर्मही कीर्णा विबर्हैरण्डजैरिव। रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गैस्तैस्तदायोधनं बभौ ॥४८॥
verses.english: The ground was then strewn over with the head-gears of those robbers and the shaved heads that looked like unfledged birds in consequence of their long beards.

verses.sanskrit: कबन्धैः संवृतं सर्वं ताम्राभ्रैः खमिवावृतम्। वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शैः सुपर्वभिरजिह्मगैः॥४९। ते सात्वतेन निहताः समावव्रुर्वसुन्धराम्। अल्पावशिष्टाः संभग्नाः कृच्छ्रमाणा विचेतसः॥५०॥
जिताः संख्ये महाराज युयुधानेन दंशिताः। पार्ष्णिभिश्च कशाभिश्च ताडयन्तस्तुरङ्गमान्॥५१॥
verses.english: The handful remnant of those mail-covered soldiers, defeated, O king, by the Satvata hero, became cheerless; and finding their lives on the points of being snatched away from them, they broke.

verses.sanskrit: जवमुत्तममास्थाय सर्वतः प्राद्रवन् भयात्। काम्बोजसैन्यं विद्राव्य दुर्जयं युधि भारत॥५२॥
verses.english: And fled away, urging, their steeds to the top of their speed, with their whips, goads & c out of great fear that then overwhelmed them.

verses.sanskrit: यवनानां च तत्सैन्यं शकानां च महद्बलम्। ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रः सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः॥५३॥
verses.english: Routing in battle the invisible Kamboja troops and 0 Bharata, the troops of the Yavanas and the mighty host of the Sakas.

verses.sanskrit: प्रविष्टस्तावकाञ्जित्वा सूतं याहीत्यचोदयत्। तत्तस्य समरे कर्म दृष्ट्वाऽन्यैरकृतं पुरा॥५४॥
verses.english: That foremost of men, viz... Satyaki of prowess incapable of being baffled, penetrated into the heart of your troops, vanquishing them and urging his charioteer saying, "Proceed."

verses.sanskrit: चारणाः सहगन्धर्वाः पूजयांचक्रिरे भृशम्। तं यान्तं पृष्ठगोप्तारमर्जुनस्य विशांपते। चारणाः प्रेक्ष्य संहृष्टास्त्वदीयाश्चाभ्यपूजयन्॥५५॥
verses.english: Then, O ruler of men, beholding him proceeding as the rear-guard of Arjuna, the Charanas were filled with delight. Even your troops then began to applaud him.
